_readme: THE SYSTEMS PANEL MANIFEST LAID AGAINST THE ENGINE'S REQUEST MODEL. TWO LISTS THAT HAD NEVER
BEEN COMPARED UNTIL 2026-09-13.
⛔ THIS FILE IS THE ONLY AUTHORED PART OF THE RECONCILIATION AND IT IS CHECKED IN BOTH
DIRECTIONS, exactly like SACRED{} and the Sacred host list: every panel leaf read off the
running Mock must appear in `panel`, and every field on the engine's request model must be
either the target of a panel row or declared in `engine_only`. A row that drifts out of
either list turns the census RED rather than quietly shrinking it.
⛔ NEITHER SIDE IS TYPED HERE. The panel side is read off window.DATUMAE_MODEL_SCHEDULE in a
real browser; the engine side is read off the running pydantic model. This file only says
what each pairing IS.
BUCKETS:
ENGINE_HAS      - the panel shows it and the engine has a field for it. `engine` names it.
ENGINE_LACKS    - the panel shows it and THE ENGINE HAS NOWHERE TO PUT IT. A build.
ALT_SPELLING    - a second spelling of another row's answer (a date beside an age, a monthly
cadence beside an annual figure). Not a separate model input; `same_as`
names the row it restates. A control here still has to agree with its twin.
DERIVED_DISPLAY - computed for the screen from answers already given, or derived inside the
engine from another field. Nothing to send.
CONFIG          - selects WHICH fields exist rather than being one of them.
MACHINERY       - infrastructure the user has no opinion about.
UI_STATE        - panel bookkeeping. Never leaves the browser.
PANEL_SILENT    - (engine_only) the engine accepts it and NO panel row shows it. This is the
bucket nobody had ever looked at.
LAW 223 COLUMN — `live` names the selector in LIVE studio.html that SETS this row, or
null when NO control exists in the product, or "DYNAMIC" when the control is created
per account (the estate rooms) rather than shipped with a fixed id.
⛔ IT IS VERIFIED IN A REAL DOM, NEVER BY SUBSTRING. "equity" appears 149 times in live
studio.html and nearly all of it is HOME equity in the property rooms — a grep would
have reported the allocation sliders as present. Law 221.

planMode.note: Solo or joint. Decides whether the co_architect_* fields exist at all, which is why the payload gate had to learn to enter dual.

co.retirementAge.note: ⛔ The engine ACCEPTS it and the product NEVER ASKS for it — no door refuses on the co-architect's retirement date. Clause 1 asymmetry. A BUILD, NEVER A DELETE (law 191).

co.planThroughAge.note: ⛔ Filled by a MIRROR that copies the primary's plan-through age, so two people are modelled as dying at the same age — against the engine's own field description, 'stated, never assumed equal'. Collapses the survivor window to zero.

co.claimAge.note: ⛔ Pre-selected in live markup and declared kind:'derived'. Nobody picks it.

tax.stateTax.note: The engine derives the state rate from location; the panel shows it back so the user can see what their answer implied.

pensionAmount.note: Household total of the two pension rows below.

pensionPrimaryAmount.note: A pension rides in as an account whose annual_contribution carries the annual income.

pensionCola.note: Household summary of the two per-person COLA rows.

pensionColaPrimary.mode.note: mode 'not_sure' is an honest empty state — it must send nothing, never 0.

pensionColaPrimary.rate.note: ⚠️ PERCENT ON SCREEN, FRACTION ON THE WIRE. 2 means 2%; the engine bounds 0..0.2. 0.2% sent unconverted arrives as 20%, sits ON the bound and PASSES.

ss.claimAge.note: ⛔ Pre-selected in live markup. Nobody picks it.

ss.haircut.note: ⛔ The engine defaults 0.0 — it assumes Social Security is never cut — and nothing on the live product shows that the position was taken. Right value, wrong address.

healthcare.preMedicare.note: Monthly on screen, annual on the wire.

healthcare.inflation.note: ⛔⛔ NO HEALTHCARE INFLATION EXISTS ANYWHERE IN THE ENGINE — measured 2026-09-13 across every module. healthcare_annual sits FLAT forever, and because the engine models real dollars that silently asserts healthcare inflates at exactly CPI. ⚠️ The panel's 4.5%/yr is NOMINAL; the field the engine needs is EXCESS OVER CPI (~2-2.5%), or general inflation is double-counted.

allocation.equity.note: STAR WIRED 2026-09-16: the household's own stock/bond/cash split reaches the engine. This row read ENGINE_LACKS for three days AFTER the field landed, which is the census's own stale-map failure: a diff is only as current as the list it diffs against. ⛔⛔ THE PRIORITY OF THE ARC. The engine has NO allocation field; it runs a hardcoded glide (GLIDE_START_EQ 0.79 -> GLIDE_END_EQ 0.50 over 30 years, CASH_PCT 0.03) sourced to the Captain's own workbook cells I&A B265-B267. ⚠️ An equity_pct PARAMETER exists but feeds only the MEAN RETURN; volatility comes from glide_vol() which reads the constants and ignores it — so wiring the obvious parameter open

allocation.bond.note: STAR WIRED 2026-09-16: the household's own stock/bond/cash split reaches the engine. This row read ENGINE_LACKS for three days AFTER the field landed, which is the census's own stale-map failure: a diff is only as current as the list it diffs against. Same wall as allocation.equity.

allocation.cash.note: STAR WIRED 2026-09-16: the household's own stock/bond/cash split reaches the engine. This row read ENGINE_LACKS for three days AFTER the field landed, which is the census's own stale-map failure: a diff is only as current as the list it diffs against. Same wall as allocation.equity. Already declared kind:'unsourced' in the engine's constant ledger with a note saying the user cannot touch it.

cape.note: A world fact. Needs a value PLUS an as-of date PLUS a staleness policy, never a bare number.

bridgeMode.note: Already a labelled dropdown in the Mock. Right value, wrong address — the default lives in schemas.py instead of on the panel.

marketModel.note: House default Datumae Blend, applied by the panel as a labelled assumption — never by a class='active' attribute.

contributions.accounts.ira.continueAfter.note: AccountInput carries type, balance, annual_contribution and rule_of_55_eligible. There is no 'keep contributing after retirement' flag; contributions accrue during accumulation only.

contributions.accounts.workplace.continu.note: Same gap as the IRA row.

contributions.accounts.taxable.continueA.note: The Mock says taxable CAN continue after retirement. The engine cannot express it.

contributionGrowth.note: ⛔ The engine models contributions as a LEVEL annuity — portfolio x growth + contribution x (growth-1)/r — so they never escalate. A 401(k) contribution tracks the limit and the salary, and the limit rises most years. The control already exists in the Mock at 0-8%, step 0.25, default 2%. Must accept 0 for a user who wants flat.

machinery.trialsPerModel.note: Shown for transparency; the engine takes one trial count.

machinery.totalPaths.note: trials x models, for the screen.

machinery.overrides.note: Reports whether any spreadsheet override is in play.

floorLoad.note: ⭐ THE DOOR LANDED 2026-09-13. Until then compute_bedrock tested all_survived as a literal, so the Ceiling was shapeable from Python and the Floor was not shapeable at any price. The engine now also returns floor_notches saying which positions leave a range to show.

specReviewed.note: Whether the user has acknowledged the panel. Never leaves the browser.

feeDrag.note: CRITICAL WIRED 2026-09-17. The panel showed a live slider labelled 'editable engine assumption' while the engine held a literal 0.00109 for every household on earth. MEASURED: a retail 1% fee costs -$5,000 to -$8,000/yr of ladder.

generalInflation.note: CRITICAL WIRED 2026-09-17. `inflation` was a function default the API could never set, so every household got 3.0%. MEASURED: one point of inflation is worth -$5,000 to -$10,000/yr of ladder.

generalInflationMode.note: The preset/fine selector in front of generalInflation. UI_STATE - the engine reads the resulting rate, never the mode that produced it.

healthcare.excessInflation.note: CRITICAL WIRED 2026-09-17 and it did not exist in the engine in any form. Stored as an EXCESS over general inflation, which is the panel's own shape ('+2.0 pts above CPI'); an absolute rate would let the two drift apart the first time somebody moved the general one. MEASURED: the panel's own +2.0 points is worth -$2,000 to -$4,000/yr. WARNING: the engine default is 0.0, not 2.0 - a dated transition object so nothing moves for a caller that has not been updated. The removal trigger is the commit that has the panel send it.

expectedReturns.equity.note: The panel exposes a nominal-return slider per asset class; the engine computes blended_nominal from HARD-CODED 0.08 / 0.045 / 0.025. Three more sliders that move nothing. Same shape as feeDrag was until today.

pensionInflationPrimary.note: Pension inflation PROTECTION (fixed vs CPI-linked), which is not the same field as pension_cola's rate. Distinct row, no engine field.

machinery.ignoredInputs.note: The engine reports fields it RECEIVED and does not model. WARNING: it is blind to the larger gap - a control the client never sends is as invisible to it as one the engine never accepts. THIS CENSUS is the instrument for that half.

machinery.bedrockStress.note: Stress battery returned by the engine. Diagnostic readout.

machinery.bridgeAccess.note: Pre-59.5 access diagnostic returned by the engine.

machinery.specVersion.note: Engine version that produced the Range. Provenance, not an input.

machinery.computationTime.note: Runtime reported by the engine. Provenance, not an input.

healthcare.irmaaEnabled.note: IRMAA — the Medicare income surcharge. RESHAPED BY THE ARCHITECT 2026-09-17 and the reshape is the finding: it was drawn PER PERSON, and it cannot be. The bracket is a JOINT income test — one household income decides the band — and the premium is then charged per person, so "model it for one spouse and not the other" IS NOT A STATE THAT EXISTS. It is now one household-level control writing this single flag. ⛔ The engine has no IRMAA at all, so this is a BUILD, and it is on the Obligation Ledger as one of the 13 absent obligations.

v257.irmaa.note: The v257 segmented control's own state ('model' / 'ignore'), which writes healthcare.irmaaEnabled. Not a second input — the same answer in the control's vocabulary. A control here still has to agree with its twin.

v257.rebalancing.note: How the stock/bond/cash mix is MAINTAINED over the horizon — hold the target / let it drift / glide to conservative. ⭐ THE ARCHITECT'S OWN ARGUMENT FOR IT IS THAT MOST OF THE VALUE IS MAKING THE DEFAULT VISIBLE: holding 80/17/3 for thirty years MEANS selling stocks and buying bonds every year, and nothing on any screen currently says that a fixed mix is a behaviour. ⛔ The engine rebalances implicitly and has no field to say otherwise.

v257.longevityPrimary.note: Fixed horizon vs modeled lifespan, for the PRIMARY. ⛔⛔ THIS IS A CLAUSE 1 ROW, NOT A SETTINGS ROW: modelled lifespan is one of the two remaining gaps on two-people-becoming-one, and it is BLOCKED ON FAILURE MAGNITUDE (§82.2727) exactly as the guardrail bands are. ⚠️ The spread is a DATED SOURCED TABLE, never a slider — a user-tuned mortality spread has no obviously wrong value, so nobody could ever tell it was working.

v257.longevityCo.note: The same control for the CO-ARCHITECT, and it is a SEPARATE ROW rather than a shared one BY THE CAPTAIN'S FIRST CLAUSE: two people have two death dates and the survivor's finances are not the couple's halved. ⚠️ Flagged by the Architect while specifying it: the panel screenshot shows CO PLAN-THROUGH AGE 107 — test data or a real entry, it is the kind of value that quietly doubles a horizon.

v257.taxSunset.note: After the sunset, assume current law continues / scheduled reversion. ⛔⛔ NOT A GENERIC CONTROL — it is the same row as the enhanced senior deduction, which EXPIRES AFTER 2028, and as the ordinary brackets. Projecting a dated rule thirty years forward is the identical defect in the identical FLATTERING direction. ⚠️ Its chip and switch copy is [COPY-OWED] to the Architect and must not be filled with placeholder wording.

v257.rothConversion.note: RULED NOT PANEL WORK by the Architect: a conversion is a DECISION, and the Systems Panel is a specification surface for assumptions. Present in the Mock as state only. ⚠️ When it is built it is a single policy selector — fill to the 12/22/24% bracket each year until RMDs begin — which the engine could answer; it CANNOT answer "should I convert this year?", which is an optimisation over a sequence of decisions and a different kind of run.

v257.healthcareArchitectView.note: Which person's healthcare figures the panel is currently SHOWING. Browser-only: it selects a view, never a fact about the household. ⚠️ Deliberately distinguished from the IRMAA row above, which LOOKS like a per-person control and is not one.

rangeTriggered.note: Whether the Reveal has been fired from the panel this session. Panel bookkeeping; never leaves the browser.

current_ss_plan.note: Marks one SS-matrix cell as the household's current plan. The SS matrix has its own surface; no Systems Panel row shows it.

custom_weights.note: Per-model blend weights for the Custom Matrix option. RULED RETIRED alongside market_outlook 'custom' — the five-button control replaces it. Still on the model.

accum_years_override.note: YEARFRAC-precise accumulation years, for exact spreadsheet cell matching. A development affordance, never a user input.

portfolio_at_retirement_override.note: Exact portfolio FV from a spreadsheet cell. Same status as accum_years_override.

target_equity_pct.note: The household's TARGET mix, as distinct from the mix they hold today. ⭐ A SECOND FACT, NOT A RESTATEMENT (2026-09-17): allocation.* says what the portfolio IS; this says what it is meant to become. The Mock's rebalancing control is the surface that will eventually set it — see v257.rebalancing, which is why these two rows must be read together and not closed separately.

target_bond_pct.note: See target_equity_pct — the bond leg of the same target mix.

target_cash_pct.note: See target_equity_pct — the cash leg of the same target mix.

allocation_classified_pct.note: ⛔⛔ WHAT SHARE OF THE PORTFOLIO THE HOUSEHOLD ACTUALLY CLASSIFIED, AND IT EXISTS TO KILL A CLIFF. `_householdAssetMix` used to return NULL below 95% coverage, so A HOUSEHOLD WHO CLASSIFIED 94% OF THEIR MONEY WAS HANDED A STRANGER'S ALLOCATION FOR ALL OF IT — silently, and failing in the worst available direction. Nobody ever ruled that threshold. MEASURED: nothing-classified keystone 126,000 against 94%-classified 137,000. The engine now blends its neutral default into the REMAINDER by value and discloses the unclassified dollars by name. ⚠️ No panel row shows it because it is not an ANSWER, it is a MEASURE OF THE ANSWER'S COVERAGE.

match_excluded_annual.note: ⛔ THE EMPLOYER MATCH WE COULD NOT COUNT because vesting is blank. Without it the engine would see a smaller contribution and report nothing — a conservative assumption with NO DISCLOSURE, which is indistinguishable from a defect (§82.2702). It travels so the answer can say what it left out. Panel-silent by nature: it is a statement about missing input, not an input.

match_salary_missing.note: The THIRD distinct match condition: a match set as a PERCENTAGE OF PAY with no pay to apply it to. Unlike the vesting-blank case there is no dollar figure to withhold — the match cannot be SIZED at all — so a flag is the only honest form. ⚠️ IT IS ONE OF THE SIX FIELDS THAT STILL CARRY A DEFAULT (False), and it is the one where the default is least arguable: absent salary genuinely is the common case.
